transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, I guess I'm here because I've been having a really hard time lately, ever since they made me the acting workflow lead at my job. 

I work at a warehouse, and lately, I just walk in the door already tense. I've been snapping at people over little SAP errors, and... I'm even missing cycle-count deadlines that I never used to miss. It's just not like me. And then when my shift is over, I go home and I'm just completely drained. I don't even have the energy to play basketball or work on my sketches anymore. It's just taking a lot out of me.

Are you feeling this way exclusively because of the pressures of your new role, or do you find yourself feeling this same level of worry and low mood even when you are away from work and not thinking about your job?

Well, honestly, I'm not entirely sure. It's... it's hard to separate it out. Even when I'm at home, the job is still kind of hanging over my head. I'm usually dreading going back in or worrying about the stuff I didn't finish. So I guess I haven't really noticed if I feel this way when I'm completely not thinking about work, just because... well, it feels like it's always on my mind right now.
Over the past few weeks, have you felt this way—the low mood and lack of interest in your hobbies—almost every single day?

Yeah, I'd say it's been pretty much every day for the last few weeks. I wake up feeling drained, and I just don't have the motivation to do anything I usually enjoy, even on my days off. It's just a constant feeling lately.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or your sleep patterns since this all started?

No, not really. My appetite is about the same as usual. I'm eating normally. And my sleep hasn't really changed either. I'm still getting my regular hours, I just... wake up feeling tired anyway. But the actual sleeping and eating parts are fine.
When you are feeling this way, do you experience a sense of nervousness, worry, or physical tension, such as a racing heart or feeling keyed up?

I wouldn't say I get a racing heart or anything like that. I mean, I definitely feel worried and kind of tense about the whole situation, but it's not like a physical panic or feeling super keyed up. It's more just a heavy, constant worry that sits with me, rather than making my body react, if that makes sense.

Looking back at your life, have you ever experienced a period of at least two weeks where you felt this same low mood and lack of interest, even when you weren't dealing with a specific stressful life event?

No, not really. I mean, looking back... I don't think I've ever had a time where I felt this down and just out of it for weeks without a reason. Usually, my mood is pretty steady unless something specific is going on. So, no, I haven't experienced anything quite like this before.
When you think about the distress you are feeling, would you say the 'low' or sad feeling is the most prominent part, or is the feeling of worry and nervousness more dominant?

I'm honestly not sure. It's hard to pick one over the other, to be honest. They kind of just... blend together for me. I definitely feel down about everything, but that heavy worry I mentioned is always there right alongside it. So I guess I don't really know which one is more dominant. It just feels like an equal mix of both.
If you had to describe your experience to a friend, would you say you feel more 'sad and hopeless' or more 'nervous and worried'?

I really couldn't say. Like I mentioned before, they just sort of happen at the same time. I don't think I could pick one over the other if I was trying to explain it to someone. It's just... both of them, equally, I guess.
